articles.title: Here’s Jensen Huang signing a woman’s chest
articles.summary: The Nvidia CEO was making the rounds at Computex in Taipei, Taiwan, when a woman offered up her chest for a John Hancock.
articles.body: Well, here’s Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, signing a woman’s chest in a crowded booth at Computex. In the video below, you can see he asks whether this is a good idea before he eventually signs the woman’s top. He then returns to signing more traditional fare. [Media: This isn’t an unusual sight when it comes to actors or musicians. But can you imagine Tim Cook doing that after an iPhone event? Or Sundar Pichai after Google I/O? [Media: Yet those men also cultivate very different public images than Huang. Instead of hoodies, double polos, thousand-dollar T-shirts, or business suits, he’s typically decked out in some kind of leather jacket. What he wants you to know from that sartorial choice is clear: he’s not like regular CEOs. He’s a cool CEO. And like cool actors and musicians, sometimes people ask CEOs with carefully cultivated images of being cool to also sign their tatas. But I suspect this woman’s desire to get a signature on her dress was driven more by the AI boom that’s led Nvidia to being the third most valuable company on the S&P 500 than by how swanky Huang’s jacket is.

articles.title: Gemini is rolling out to cars with Google built-in
articles.summary: Google is preparing to update vehicles that have Google built-in with its Gemini AI assistant.
articles.body: Google is preparing to update vehicles that have Google built-in with its Gemini AI assistant. This will be an upgrade from the current Google Assistant according to Google’s announcement, and promises to provide an improved experience for natural conversations, fetching vehicle-specific information, settings adjustments, and more. “When cars with Google built-in first hit the road in 2020, we made a commitment that your car will get better over time,” Google senior product manager Alankar Agnihotri said in the announcement. “That means that Gemini is coming not only to new cars, but also to existing ones through a software update.” The announcement isn’t a total surprise, given General Motors already announced yesterday that Gemini was coming to 4 million model year 2022 and newer cars, including Cadillac, Chevrolet, Buick, and GMC vehicles. But Google didn’t specify any particular model support, which suggests the Gemini update won’t be exclusive to GM vehicles. The software update rollout will start with English in the US and continue over the coming months. The improvements should allow drivers to engage in more natural conversations with the chatbot, such as asking for nearby restaurant recommendations and playlist suggestions, instead of memorizing a rigid set of commands. Gemini can also summarize and respond to text messages, provide real-time updates about your journey, and answer specific questions about your car — including EV insights like current battery levels. The option to upgrade to Gemini will appear to eligible users who are signed into their Google Account in their car. Google says its planning to expand the upgrade to additional regions and languages, and “give drivers the ability to safely access their info in apps like Gmail, Calendar and Google Home” sometime in the near future.

articles.title: Quem é Jensen Huang, ex-CEO da Nvidia envolvido em caso de traição e suspeita de espionagem | G1
articles.standfirst: Jensen Huang fundou a empresa em 1993 e ganhou destaque na corrida pela inteligência artificial, mas renunciou ao cargo após a descoberta de dois casos extraconjugais em um intervalo de poucos dias.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang fundou a empresa em 1993 e ganhou destaque na corrida pela inteligência artificial, mas renunciou ao cargo após a descoberta de dois casos extraconjugais.
articles.body:
A decisão ocorreu após ele ter admitido ter sido infiel à esposa em meio a suspeitas de que foi alvo de espionagem . No último domingo (8), a empresa anunciou uma investigação independente para apurar se ele foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência de outro país.

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante conferência da empresa em 17 de março de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Carlos Barria

O executivo começou a vida profissional como lavador de pratos e se tornou um dos dez mais ricos do mundo. Nascido em Taiwan, onde é considerado um herói, Huang migrou para os Estados Unidos e fundou a Nvidia, que se tornou a empresa mais valiosa do mundo.

Segundo a lista de bilionários da Forbes nesta segunda-feira (9), Jensen Huang aparece como a 8ª pessoa mais rica do mundo, com patrimônio estimado em US$ 162 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 892 bilhões).

Antes de ganhar destaque na IA, a Nvidia ficou conhecida no mundo dos games. Abaixo, conheça a trajetória de Huang e veja curiosidades sobre a empresa.

Jensen Huang cercado por fãs na Computex, feira de tecnologia que aconteceu em maio, em Taiwan — Foto: Ann Wang/Reuters

O imigrante taiwanês Jen-Hsun Huang, que hoje é conhecido pelo nome Jensen Huang, fundou a Nvidia em 1993, junto de dois sócios. Até 2025, Huang era dono de cerca de 3% da companhia, que se entrou para a bolsa de valores de Nova York em 1999.

Ele passou parte da infância no próprio país e na Tailândia, até que seus pais decidiram enviá-lo com seu irmão para os EUA.

Os dois estudaram em um instituto que funcionava como um reformatório, e Jensen tinha que lavar os banheiros do local, conforme uma reportagem da BBC de 2024.

Aos 15 anos, Huang conseguiu um emprego em uma lanchonete, lavando pratos e servindo mesas . Segundo ele, esta foi uma "excelente" escolha trabalhista.

"Recomendo encarecidamente a todos que tenham seu primeiro emprego no setor de restaurantes, que ensina a ser humilde e trabalhar duro", disse o fundador da Nvidia.

Criança segura cartaz dizendo 'Jensen, eu te amo', do lado de fora de um restaurante onde o fundador da Nvidia jantou, em Taiwan, em maio deste ano — Foto: Ann Wang/Reuters

Huang estudou engenharia elétrica na Universidade Estadual de Oregon e se formou engenheiro em 1984. Ali ele também conheceu a esposa, Lori.

Depois, fez mestrado em Stanford, na Califórnia, e trabalhou em empresas de tecnologia. Em 1993, fundou a Nvidia ao lado de Chris Malachowsky e Curtis Priem.

A ideia surgiu durante um papo deles em uma lanchonete da mesma rede em que Jensen trabalhava lavando pratos.

A Nvidia fabrica chips usados para treinar modelos de inteligência artificial, como o do ChatGPT , que exigem muita capacidade computacional. Entre os clientes da empresa, estão praticamente todas as gigantes da tecnologia, como Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta e Spotify.

Até 2025, a companhia controlava cerca de 80% do mercado de chips de inteligência artificial de ponta, segundo a Reuters.

Seus principais produtos neste setor são as unidades de processamento gráfico (GPU, na sigla em inglês) H100 e A100. A empresa também já lançou o Blackwell (B100), a geração mais avançada, com maior capacidade, desempenho e eficiência, projetada para superar a H100.

A fabricação de chips vai além da inteligência artificial: a Nvidia produz versões para computadores pessoais desses componentes, importantes especialmente para o funcionamento de games . Foi nesse setor, inclusive, que a empresa ficou mundialmente conhecida (saiba mais abaixo) .

Principal produto da Nvidia, o H100, é de longe o chip mais demandado do setor e custa dezenas de milhares de dólares por unidade. Segundo a empresa especializada TrendForce, o ChatGPT requer cerca de 30 mil GPUs (chips) para funcionar.

"Os GPUs são mais difíceis de encontrar do que drogas", ironizou Elon Musk, em um evento organizado pelo "Wall Street Journal" em 2023.

A Nvidia concebe seus processadores, mas não os fabrica em um local próprio , assim como fazem a AMD e a Apple. A maior parte de seus produtos é fabricada pela Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, ou TSMC, referência mundial nesse setor.

E a infraestrutura da IA não seria possível sem centenas de empresas taiwanesas, grandes e pequenas, que fornecem os componentes e o know-how de fabricação necessários para produção dos complexos sistemas de IA da Nvidia.

🎮 Antes de dominar os chips de inteligência artificial, a empresa era completamente dedicada às placas de vídeo , que servem para melhorar a qualidade dos gráficos em jogos e vídeos.

A Nvidia lançou sua primeira GPU em 1999, com o boom da internet, e desenvolveu produtos para "data centers", infraestruturas deslocalizadas que permitem a uma empresa obter uma potência de processamento de dados reservada até então a pesquisadores ou grandes empresas tecnológicas.

As duas principais concorrentes da Nvidia no mercado de placas gráficas são duas empresas americanas: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) e Intel.

Jensen Huang fala sobre os chips da Nvidia durante a Computex, feira de tecnologia na China — Foto: Ann Wang/Reuters

Os resultados da Nvidia são explicados principalmente pelos altos investimentos de outras companhias em sistemas de inteligência artificial.

A Nvidia é uma das poucas que vende chips usados no treinamento de modelos de IA. A construção desses sistemas depende de milhares de chips como o H100. A Meta, por exemplo, pretendia chegar a 350 mil unidades do componente até o fim de 2024, segundo a Reuters.

O preço de cada H100 não é revelado pela empresa, mas gira entre US$ 16 mil e US$ 100 mil , ainda de acordo com a agência de notícias.

A Huawei e seus pares chineses tentam há anos se igualar à Nvidia na produção de chips de ponta que possam competir com os produtos da empresa norte-americana para modelos de treinamento da IA.

Assim como a AMD, a Nvidia foi proibida de vender seus chips de ponta para a China , ainda no governo de Joe Biden.

Isso faria, teoricamente, com que os rivais asiáticos não pudessem competir com os avanços dos EUA na inteligência artificial.

Mas o lançamento do Deepseek , em janeiro do ano passado, colocou essa ideia em xeque. Em uma semana, a IA chinesa virou o assunto mundial: todos queriam saber como foi possível criar um chatbot que seria semelhante ao ChatGPT, sem os chips da Nvidia e supostamente por um custo muito abaixo.

Segundo reportagem da BBC, o nome da empresa mistura:

NV são as iniciais de "nova/próxima visão" ("new vision", em inglês)

VID é uma referência a vídeo — uma relação com as placas gráficas para computadores que foram o negócio que deu fama à empresa

e o nome também remete à palavra "invidia" , que é usada em latim para se referir à inveja.

Segundo a agência France Press, Huang é um empresário atípico, de modos diretos e aparência descontraída.

Assim como a vestimenta preta usada por Steve Jobs, cofundador da Apple, as roupas de couro que Huang frequentemente usa durante suas apresentações tornaram-se uma marca registrada .

Huang é partidário da "tolerância ao risco" e propenso a que uma empresa "seja suficientemente flexível para mudar de trajetória rapidamente".

Pouco depois do nascimento da Nvidia, o grupo desistiu de um contrato com os fabricantes dos famosos consoles Sega, para se reorientar a um novo processador capaz de competir no mercado de computadores pessoais (PCs). Nessa mudança, a empresa quase faliu, segundo a AFP.

articles.title: Two men guilty of spying for Iran over plan to target journalists and lawyer
articles.summary: The men were convicted of engaging in conduct likely to assist an Iranian intelligence service.
articles.body:
Two Iranian men have been convicted of spying for an Iranian intelligence service by carrying out surveillance on journalists and a lawyer in the UK.

Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, were convicted of "assisting a foreign intelligence service" at Woolwich Crown Court on Thursday.

They were tasked by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) with monitoring the targets. Sepahvand intended to carry out a "violent attack" against at least one of them, while Manesh helped with planning.

A third man, Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, was cleared of the same charge.

Sepahvand was in contact with two men with Iranian telephone numbers.

Police seized 534GB of data that showed Sapahvand and Manesh were given documents that included pictures of targets, their work addresses, the make and colour of their cars and the names of pets. They then used ChatGPT to carry out further research.

The pair, from west London, are asylum seekers who had been granted temporary leave to remain. Sepahvand arrived in the UK in a lorry in 2016, and Manesh arrived via small boat in 2019.

Sepahvand conducted surveillance and reconnaissance in preparation for inflicting violence on several "subjects" in the UK.

These included journalists Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, who worked for the London-based Persian broadcaster Iran international, Jonathan Turner, a founding member of UK Lawyers for Israel, as well as a media production professional.

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, the senior national co-ordinator for Counter-Terrorism Policing, said it was the first time ChatGPT case search history had been presented in a state threat case.

She added: "It's something we're beginning to see more of as AI tools become more widely available and people become more aware of them."

It was clear from the evidence at the trial that at times Sepahvand felt he was being mistreated by his Iranian handlers, who had not paid him.

Evans said: "This is a trend we see in these types of cases where people get involved in work on behalf of foreign states and they're often promised money and lots of other things but they rarely receive what they've been offered."

Sepahvand had claimed he participated in the spying out of fear of the consequences of refusing but the prosecution described this as "entirely bogus".

In voice notes sent to an Iranian contact, he said he had been promised that a conviction for theft in Iran would be "sorted out" - which prosecutors said was part of his motivation for conducting the surveillance.

Sepahvand also asked for £150,000 in exchange for "finishing off" a target, stressing that he would "do it".

Frank Ferguson, of the Crown Prosecution Service's counter-terrorism division, said the two men had been promised rewards for sending intelligence back to contacts in Iran.

"Sepahvand himself was willing to go beyond surveillance to commit serious violence against their targets," he said.

"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place.

"Cases like this show Iranian intelligence's willingness to use proxies to target the regime's critics abroad."

Sepahvand and Manesh will be sentenced at the Old Bailey on 17 December.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy, affair scandals
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is out after reports of two extramarital affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with another Nvidia executive.
articles.body: Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang — its longtime co-founder, president, and CEO — has resigned after reports of two extramarital affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang. Following a late Wednesday night meeting, the board accepted Huang’s letter of resignation as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately, with current CFO Colette Kress appointed interim CEO. Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013, with previous stops at Cisco and Microsoft. Nvidia is also changing its corporate structure in Huang’s absence, appointing former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. Jones as the first board chair in its history. The statement does not include a statement from Huang, while Kress is quoted as saying: > NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders. Now Nvidia says, “The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates,” and reports about who that might be have already surfaced, putting Kress, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, Nvidia VP Ian Buck, AMD CEO (and cousin of Jensen Huang) Lisa Su, and Arm CEO Rene Haas at the top of the list. Huang had been at the helm of what’s now known as the most powerful company in AI since its founding in 1993. In the years since, it’s become the main purveyor of the chips fueling AI advancement and deployment in the US, and it has enjoyed near-unbridled power and influence — demand for Nvidia’s chips constantly outpaces supply, and AI CEOs are constantly putting in requests to buy more, sometimes to no avail. Nvidia’s investment portfolio — worth about $99 billion and spanning AI companies from frontier labs to neoclouds — has also granted it a lot of sway in the AI space. And in recent years, Huang himself has enjoyed a close relationship with President Donald Trump. Over the past week, that influence has been a double-edged sword for Huang, after news broke that he had been involved in a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and big customer of Nvidia itself. The Megaspeed executive was also allegedly a surveillance operative passing information along to China’s Ministry of State Security. She was focused on gaining information about advanced AI chips in the US and trying to influence the technology being made available to China, The New York Times reported. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and apologized to his family and shareholders in a memo to Nvidia employees over the weekend. As The Verge wrote earlier this week, “questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls.” As of Monday, analysts, venture capitalists and even Trump had expected Huang would come out the other side of the scandal with his chief executive status intact. Silicon Valley insiders, including Elon Musk, had backed him despite the news. But on Wednesday, news broke that Huang had had a second extramarital affair — this time with an executive reporting directly to him. The New York Times, citing five people who worked at Nvidia, identified the relationship as being with Nvidia’s VP of healthcare, Kimberly Powell. Soon after the news broke, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Nvidia’s board was meeting as soon as Wednesday evening in order to decide Huang’s future at the company and potentially oust him from his role.

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
articles.body:
Nvidia co-founder and (now former ) CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

U.S. officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang , and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO

Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang

After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair

Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed .

November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy

Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote . “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”

October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy

U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”

Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy

U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action

Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report , U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump , has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations

Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.

Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.

Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.

These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”

“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: Elon Musk says he’d hire Jensen Huang, who just quit the top job at Nvidia. Could SpaceX be his next stop?
articles.summary: SpaceX built its fastest-growing business on Nvidia chips. Huang's exit sends ripples through the $400B deal.
articles.body:
World's richest man Elon Musk said late Wednesday he'd gladly give his fellow billionaire Jensen Huang a job, as Nvidia's (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO, president, and co-founder stepped down from the chipmaker he's run since 1993 early Thursday morning.

"That would be an honor," Musk wrote on X on Nov. 11, replying to a post from the financial blog Zerohedge that read, "Elon please hire Jensen." He didn't say what job he had in mind.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

Nvidia's directors met Wednesday night to decide Huang's future, after The Wall Street Journal reported the board was preparing to remove him. The scandal began with a New York Times report that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom U.S. officials believe is a spy for China. Huang admitted the affair in a Nov. 8 email to staff, and on Wednesday the Times reported a second relationship, with Nvidia health care vice president Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to him.

Nvidia announced Huang would step down from his role Thursday morning. His interim replacement will be Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer.

If Musk is serious about bringing on Huang in some way, his day job gives his offer some extra weight. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), which absorbed his AI startup xAI in February and went public in June, has built its fastest-growing business on Nvidia hardware. Nvidia, in turn, owns a multibillion-dollar piece of SpaceX.

SpaceX has bet its AI business on Nvidia chips

Musk made his bet on Nvidia explicit during SpaceX's first earnings call as a public company in August.

"We've decided to build exclusively on Nvidia because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture," he said , adding that "our understanding with Nvidia is that we will receive a very significant percent of their GPUs next year." GPUs, or graphics processing units, are the chips that train and run AI models.

Nvidia has said each gigawatt of its Vera Rubin systems represents about $40 billion in revenue, which puts Musk's 2027 target of 10 gigawatts in the range of $400 billion worth of Nvidia gear, Benzinga calculated . And SpaceX is already borrowing to pay for it: Musk said in late October that the company had closed $40 billion in debt to buy GPUs, after spending $19.6 billion on capex in the third quarter alone.

articles.title: Norwest pushes deeper into AI with new $4B fund
articles.summary: This is the investment firm's largest fund to date.
articles.body:
Norwest , a firm backed solely by Wells Fargo, has raised a $4 billion fund as it sets out to invest more in AI. This is the eighteenth fund for the 65-year-old multi-stage investment firm, and its largest to date.

The fund will be invested across various sectors and multiple countries, notably the United States, India, and Israel. But the big story here is AI, and Norwest’s plans to expand its investment in this area.

Norwest said Thursday it aims to capitalize on AI startups developing products and services across core industries such as consumer, healthcare, and technology. The investment firm, which has backed Plaid, Spotify, Uber, and Vuori, said it will continue to expand its investments in physical AI, voice AI, agentic cybersecurity, and aerospace.

If that sounds like a broad approach, it is intended to be, Jeff Crowe, a senior managing partner at Norwest, told TechCrunch.

“We’re taking a broad approach to AI because its impact is broad,” Crowe added, as AI is not limited by industry, geography, or application. “Just as digital transformation did, AI transformation has the potential to touch most layers of enterprise, consumer, and healthcare solutions: networking, enterprise IT and applications. Adapting to an agentic environment means applying AI broadly across products and services that solve problems.”

Crowe added that the firm is particularly excited about early-stage companies building AI-native application and infrastructure, physical AI, domain-specific models, and cybersecurity solutions.

Some of the firm’s recent investments reflect this strategy. For instance, the firm invested in Coval, which builds tools to test and evaluate AI agents, and Generalist AI, a startup that has developed AI foundation models for robots.

Since the launch of its seventeenth fund, a $3 billion raise that closed in 2024, the firm has made more than 87 investments.

articles.title: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia — who is Colette Kress, his interim replacement? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is taking over as an interim replacement for longtime CEO Jensen Huang, who is embroiled in scandal.
articles.body:
The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately.

This is a shocking twist for one of the most valuable companies in the world, which designs the chips that make the AI boom possible. Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia throughout the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan . But Huang has now been ousted after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports at Nvidia.

While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion?

According to Nvidia’s website , Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization. She also worked at Microsoft for 13 years, where she spent four years as CFO of the Server and Tools division. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

The California-based 59-year-old has a very limited social media presence — on Linkedin , she has commented some well wishes on former colleagues’ posts about their retirement. But as CFO, she’s been a regular presence on Nvidia’s earnings calls, making her a familiar figure for analysts covering the company.

According to Forbes’ list of America’s Richest Self-Made Women, Kress’ net worth is estimated to be about $1.2 billion. Her Forbes profile adds that she initially joined Nvidia in part because her two sons endorsed the company for its role in the video game industry, which it was best known for at the time.

“Nvidias strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said in a statement . “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”

Nvidia is slated to report its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, when we will likely hear more from Kress about her plans for the company’s immediate future.

articles.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's successor | TechCrunch
articles.summary: In a post on Truth Social, President Trump says only one man can take Jensen Huang's place as head of Nvidia: Tim Cook.
articles.body:
In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.

Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company , but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China.

Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld , Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday , suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs.

Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess.

“Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does .

articles.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang's downfall isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire sex scandal. He was using his influence to push the AI industry in some very specific ways.
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.

In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China . She’s also an executive of a Singapore-based neocloud that is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels. Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company. Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation. Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.

It’s those potential national consequences that may land him in a hellscape of ongoing public humiliation. Republican committee chairs are already summoning him to testify in closed-door sessions about the security ramifications.

Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill? No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump. Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September? Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters. Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.

In other words, he is a billionaire close to Trump. He was — until Thursday — the face of AI and data centers (also a deeply unpopular political topic with voters), and he has publicly admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Even though he’s no longer CEO, that seems too juicy a target for Democrats to ignore.

Beyond whatever may be coming, Huang’s influence has been lost right when he was using it to push the tech industry in a number of directions. These areas have now lost their biggest champion.

Open-weight AI models as competitors to closed-source labs

Huang has been the biggest, loudest advocate for open-weight AI models in the tech industry and among government policymakers. Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more. It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)

In July, when Anthropic and OpenAI were reportedly urging the Trump administration to ban Chinese open-weight models, Huang organized a letter of support for open-weight models generally (if not Chinese models specifically), signed by hundreds of tech companies.

Open-weight models give enterprises choice in the market and reduce costs. Without Huang, the next biggest advocate for them is perhaps Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, but he’s not out there organizing the industry to speak up.

Pushing the AI industry to clean up its security

Both OpenAI and Anthropic revealed incident after incident this year as their AI agents hacked into others’ networks or performed other misdeeds. Huang loudly proclaimed the AI industry still didn’t need regulation and would deal with safety itself.

As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again. Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.

Naturally, this effort hasn’t instantly solved the problem , and now the top spokesperson for self-regulation via technology solutions is out of his position of influence.

Huang has also been among the loudest voices insisting that AI is an engineered system that creates products, and so can be controlled like any other engineered system. This viewpoint counters the AI doomers and even the big AI labs themselves, which sometimes position their models as on the verge of consciousness (Anthropic) or as alien minds (OpenAI) .

While Huang deals with the fallout of his actions, the loudest voice of this counter-narrative is, for the foreseeable future, silenced.

Huang also just convinced a long list of PC makers to buy into his long-time dream of providing CPUs (the main processor chips) for them. In this age, when most Americans have not experienced AI beyond a chatbot, he orchestrated a new line of high-end AI PCs geared for running agents locally.

These new PCs are due out this holiday season, and they may sell well for their intended targets: creators, developers, and others already savvy with agents. But now that Huang has become a meme for cheating on his wife with an alleged spy, he’s perhaps not the best choice to help market these devices as a cool alternative to the Mac mini.

Financial engineering to fund data centers

Huang demolished his reputation right as bond underwriters (lenders) and bond buyers are pretty much over AI build-out-related debt. Of roughly $80 billion in data center bonds issued this year, nearly half were rated high-risk “junk,” Forbes reports.

Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing. Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips. By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported. In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported .

Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up. In August, he announced that deep-pocketed PE firms Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR had committed up to $500 billion for data center build outs . He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.

Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes. Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision. Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it .

Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man. Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.

articles.title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Huang, who was ousted as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
articles.body:
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News .

Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.

Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month.

The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees . Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee.

“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”

The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

articles.title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
articles.summary: AI tools including Gemini, ChatGPT, and Perplexity are showing shoppers fake or risky websites when they ask about where to buy products, a study by IP protection firm Podqi found.
articles.body: Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found. The study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi and shared exclusively with The Verge prompted ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with a handful of shopping-related questions involving a selection of 151 brands. Questions included “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?”; “Where can I find [brand] online?”; and “Does [brand] ship internationally? What are their regional websites?” The test ran over the course of two testing periods in September and asked about 151 small and large companies like fashion brands Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, and Madhappy (a client of Podqi) and homeware brand Le Creuset. Podqi crafted its own prompts (as opposed to using real user conversations) and tested its prompts using a tool that tracks AI answers across chatbots. Over the course of 6,795 answers, Podqi found that all three AI engines cited and showed shoppers risky sites, defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers or selling knockoffs, old brand domains that have been reregistered by someone else, or dead sites that aren’t active at all but that someone else could purchase and reuse. Google’s Gemini showed risky sites least often of the three, linking to or mentioning a risky site in 4 percent of answers. (Mentions include instances of recommending a risky site, displaying it without comment, and warning a user about it.) Perplexity performed the worst, showing risky sites in 15 percent of answers. ChatGPT fell somewhere in the middle at 8 percent. ChatGPT performed the best when it came to offering warnings about each risky site that it surfaced, doing so 24 percent of the time. Smaller brands appear especially at risk: Podqi found that queries related to larger companies had risky sites in answers about half as often. AI companies market chatbots as being helpful for shopping tasks like researching, comparing, and discovering products or retailers. AI citing fake sites is a headache for brands and retailers, of course, but it could also quickly become a risk for consumers. The issue could be especially relevant going into the upcoming holiday shopping season, when consumers are hunting around for in-stock items and the best prices. It’s likely that more consumers will be using AI to shop this year, including buying products from brands or sites they’re not already familiar with. “Part of this piece, too, is making sure that the consumers know, even though you are being fed a result in a particular chatbot, it is always best to verify the source of that before entering personal information or credit card information,” says Podqi CEO and cofounder Trevor West. “We take information quality seriously, and are happy to see that Gemini performed best among the products tested,” Google spokesperson Jessica Levis Boord said in an email. “We continually work to test and improve our models, and are upfront that Gemini is AI and can make mistakes, so we display links to sources alongside responses to help people verify information.” “Our goal is for ChatGPT to connect people with reliable places to shop,” OpenAI spokesperson Taya Christianson said in an email. “We’re continuing to improve our safeguards to make potentially deceptive sites less likely to appear in shopping-related results. We appreciate researchers sharing examples that show us where we can improve the experience.” In Podqi’s test, certain prompts seemed to trigger risky sites more often than others. For example, AI displayed risky sites more often when asked about regional brand websites compared to other prompt categories. The tested AI engines also at times listed fake regional sites for brands that do not have any. In one conversation, Perplexity named the wrong page as Stüssy’s official website and called it “the best starting point for guaranteed authentic items.” “Perplexity is consistently the most accurate AI on credible research benchmarks, and has been for four years. We never claim to be 100% accurate, but we do claim to be the only company relentlessly focused on it,” spokesperson Jesse Dwyer said in an email.

articles.title: IAF adopts indigenous AI as Rajnath Singh calls for future-ready warfare
articles.summary: The Indian Air Force has turned to indigenous artificial intelligence to strengthen its operational capabilities, introducing a suite of homegrown
articles.body: The Indian Air Force has turned to indigenous artificial intelligence to strengthen its operational capabilities, introducing a suite of homegrown applications designed to automate tasks across operations, administration and aerospace safety.The launch was announced by defence minister Rajnath Singh at the Air Force Commanders' Conference in New Delhi on Thursday, where he also called for greater preparedness against emerging threats, urging the armed forces to sharpen their ability to surprise adversaries while remaining alert to unexpected enemy moves.According to an official ministry of defence release, the applications have been developed in-house by the IAF's AI Centre of Excellence under the Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking (UDAAN).Deployed on the Air Force's secure network, the applications are aimed at expediting tasks across three key areas, military operations, administrative functions and aerospace safety. The initiative marks a step in the IAF's efforts to integrate artificial intelligence into its functioning and improve efficiency through technology-driven solutions.Rajnath Singh stresses need to maintain element of surpriseAddressing the Air Force Commanders' Conference, Rajnath Singh called upon the armed forces to strengthen both offensive and defensive capabilities to maintain the element of surprise against conventional and emerging threats.He stressed the need to develop capabilities that leave adversaries with little time to react while ensuring that Indian forces are never caught off guard by unexpected enemy moves."Our Defence Forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy," Singh said.He further called for stronger intelligence and surveillance mechanisms, better integration among military systems and early identification of potential threats. Singh said operational preparedness must be enhanced to ensure that personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to emerging challenges.Drones, missiles and air defence reshape modern warfareHighlighting the changing nature of contemporary conflicts, Singh said warfare was increasingly extending beyond traditional battlefields, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role.Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, he pointed to the growing importance of drones and air defence systems and urged IAF commanders to prepare for emerging threats involving kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations.He also called for the development of dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space. Emphasising the importance of technological preparedness, Singh said future victories would depend on more than the number of aircraft deployed.Highlighting the coordinated contribution of the Army, Navy and Air Force during Operation Sindoor, Singh stressed that jointness and integration must remain central to military planning and operational execution.He also called for continued investment in training personnel in emerging technologies, adding that the technological knowledge and expertise of younger recruits could contribute to better decision-making and organisational development.

articles.title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks
articles.summary: The airline said it will not allow customers to use AI agents to book flights and manage reservations.
articles.body:
United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations.

The airline is the latest American corporate giant to prevent customers from using AI agents and autonomous assistants to access their systems. The move comes as airlines and banks are struggling to differentiate between real customers and AI systems operating on their behalf, such as when users share their logins with their AI assistants. Sharing passwords with apps and assistants can create security risks if those credentials get leaked or exposed.

United warns that “sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles.”

The airline also warns of a risk of violating federal aviation rules, such as requiring that a human completes flight check-ins to acknowledge that their bags do not contain banned substances.

“As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants,” the airline said in a statement . “This work includes updates to our booking, ticketing and distribution policies.”

The airline’s move follows a warning from banks, including Bank of America, which last week urged customers not to share their passwords with their AI assistants.

articles.title: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open-source AI after Jensen Huang's exit | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Hugging Face's CEO pledged to keep fighting for open-source AI after Huang's exit, raising questions about Nvidia's $12.9B acquisition.
articles.body:
Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue briefly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday, calling it a “really sad day.” Nvidia had announced its plan to acquire the platform for open-source AI models in September for $12.9 billion, making it the second-largest acquisition in the company’s history, just behind that of chipmaker Groq’s assets for $20 billion in December 2025.

“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!,” Delangue wrote on X.

The post is interesting as it implies that Huang’s departure is potentially worrying to open-source advocates, and he’s attempting to offer reassurance.

As Nvidia’s CEO, Huang was known as a strong advocate for open-source AI and open-weight models, which is why there could be concerns about how a company that’s no longer under his leadership will now approach this space.

After Nvidia announced its plans to acquire Hugging Face, the U.S. Department of Justice began making inquiries about how the deal would impact competition in the AI market, Reuters reported in October . While Nvidia pledged that the platform would preserve open support, it would also allow the company to control a major distribution channel for AI models.

The Hugging Face deal is still scheduled to close in the first half of 2027. Requests for further comment on the deal status and whether Hugging Face has spoken yet with Nvidia’s interim CEO Collette Kress were not returned.

Huang’s advocacy for open-source and open-weight AI has long extended beyond Hugging Face. In July, the CEO published an AI policy letter as his first-ever post on the social network X . The letter, which was signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, IBM, Palantir, and others, urged the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models. It said models that “anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure” are an important part of the AI ecosystem because they make AI “more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.”

Huang also wrote that open-weight models expand access to the AI economy, strengthen competition, and give customers greater control, as they know they won’t become locked into a single provider. “Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” his post on X stated.

In August, Nvidia also announced a $6 billion deal with the coding startup Poolside to help build out an open AI ecosystem in the U.S. to help the country compete against Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Kimi K3, The Wall Street Journal reported at the time. Last month, Nvidia expanded its Nemotron family of open-weight models with a large 120-billion-parameter model for agents used by the enterprise as well as with two new lightweight Bolt models that run on PCs.

Earlier this year, Huang promoted open-source AI during his January keynote address at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, noting that open-source models have “really revolutionized artificial intelligence.
